items.q: Five replicate determinations of copper in an alloy gave the percentages 11.03, 11.19, 15.03, 15.12, 18.6. Calculate the median percentage.
items.s: Arranged in order the values are 11.03, 11.19, 15.03, 15.12, 18.6, so the middle value is 15.03 per cent.

items.q: A solution transmits 80 per cent of the radiation at 520 nm. Calculate its absorbance.
A solution has an absorbance of 0.44 at 460 nm. Calculate the percentage of the incident radiation transmitted.
items.s: Transmittance = 10^(-A) x 100 = 10^(-0.44) x 100 = 36.31 per cent.

items.q: A volume of 75 cm3 of a solution that is 0.101 mol/dm3 in a compound of molar mass 40 g/mol is evaporated to dryness. Calculate the mass of residue in g.
A mass of 3.39 mg of an ion is present in 200 cm3 of solution. Calculate the concentration in parts per million, that is mg per dm3.
items.s: Concentration = 3.39 mg / (200/1000) dm3 = 16.95 ppm.

items.q: A titration required 16.8 cm3 of a titrant of concentration 0.195 mol/dm3. Calculate the amount of titrant used in moles.
items.s: Moles = concentration x volume in dm3 = 0.195 x 16.8/1000 = 0.0033 mol.

items.q: A 24 cm3 aliquot of a solution of concentration 0.269 mol/dm3 is taken. Calculate the amount of solute in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles = concentration x volume in cm3 = 0.269 x 24 = 6.46 mmol.

items.q: A solution of a strong monobasic acid has a hydrogen ion concentration of 0.0025 mol/dm3. Calculate its pH.
A solution has a pH of 3.2. Calculate the hydrogen ion concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Hydrogen ion concentration = 10^(-pH) = 10^(-3.2) = 0.0006 mol/dm3.

items.q: A precipitate of mass 0.505 g was obtained whose gravimetric factor, converting the weighed form to the sought substance, is 0.75. Calculate the mass of the sought substance in g.
items.s: Mass sought = mass weighed x gravimetric factor = 0.505 x 0.75 = 0.379 g.

items.q: Two half cells have standard potentials of 0.55 V and 0.1 V. Calculate the standard cell potential obtained by coupling them.
items.s: The couple with the higher potential acts as the cathode, so the cell potential is 0.55 - (0.1) = 0.45 V.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of iron in an ore gave the percentages 15.76, 17.66, 18.18, 19.63, 15.23. Calculate the standard deviation of the results in per cent.
items.s: The mean is 17.29; the sum of squared deviations is 12.99; dividing by four and taking the root gives 1.8 per cent.

items.q: Six replicate measurements of a titre gave a mean of 35 cm3 and a standard deviation of 0.4 cm3. Calculate the relative spread of the results in per cent.
items.s: Relative spread = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (0.4/35) x 100 = 1.14 per cent.

items.q: A mean of 35 mg was obtained from 6 replicate determinations whose standard deviation was 1.13 mg. Taking the Student t value for the stated degrees of freedom as 2.31, calculate the half width of the 95 per cent confidence interval in mg.
items.s: Half width = t x standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 2.31 x 1.13 / sqrt(6) = 1.07 mg.

items.q: Four replicate results arranged in ascending order are 32, 35, 36 and 37. The first result is suspected of being an outlier. Using Q = gap / spread, calculate the rejection quotient.
items.s: Q = (second value - first value)/(largest - smallest) = (35 - 32)/(37 - 32) = 0.6.

items.q: The mean of 6 replicate determinations is 19.53 mg and their standard deviation is 0.8 mg, while the certified value for the material is 20.09 mg. Calculate the value of t.
items.s: t = |mean - certified| x sqrt(n) / standard deviation = 0.56 x sqrt(6) / 0.8 = 1.71.

items.q: The result of a determination is calculated as the product of two measured quantities whose relative uncertainties are 1.4 per cent and 1 per cent. Calculate the relative uncertainty of the result in per cent.
items.s: For a product the relative uncertainties combine in quadrature: sqrt(1.4^2 + 1^2) = 1.72 per cent.

items.q: A solution is 0.0005 mol/dm3 in a coloured species whose molar absorptivity is 3484 dm3 mol-1 cm-1; the absorbance was measured in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the absorbance.
items.s: A = absorptivity x concentration x path length = 3484 x 0.0005 x 1.00 = 1.74.

items.q: A solution of a species whose molar absorptivity is 3074 dm3 mol-1 cm-1 gives an absorbance of 0.883 in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: c = A / (absorptivity x path length) = 0.883 / (3074 x 1.00) = 0.0003 mol/dm3.

items.q: A solution of concentration 0.0004 mol/dm3 gives an absorbance of 0.877 in a cell of path length 1 cm. Calculate the molar absorptivity in dm3 mol-1 cm-1.
items.s: Absorptivity = A / (c x b) = 0.877 / (0.0004 x 1) = 2088 dm3 mol-1 cm-1.

items.q: A calibration line of absorbance against concentration passes through the standard points (0.002 mol/dm3, 0.124) and (0.008 mol/dm3, 0.511). A sample gives an absorbance of 0.279. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.
A mass of 3.69 g of a compound of molar mass 40 g/mol is dissolved in water and made up to 250 cm3. Calculate the molar concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles = 3.69/40 = 0.092; concentration = moles/(250/1000) = 0.369 mol/dm3.

items.q: 44 cm3 of a solution of concentration 0.767 mol/dm3 is diluted with water to a final volume of 250 cm3. Calculate the concentration of the diluted solution in mol/dm3.
A standard solution of concentration 0.14 mol/dm3 is to be prepared in a 1000 cm3 volumetric flask from a solid of molar mass 84 g/mol. Calculate the mass of solid required in g.
A buffer is made from a weak acid of pKa 7.35 and its sodium salt, the ratio of salt concentration to acid concentration being 4. Calculate the pH of the buffer.
items.s: pH = pKa + log(salt/acid) = 7.35 + log(4) = 7.95.

items.q: A buffer of pH 6.61 is required from a weak acid of pKa 6.01. Calculate the ratio of the concentration of the conjugate base to that of the acid.
items.s: From pH = pKa + log(ratio), log(ratio) = 6.61 - 6.01, so the ratio is 3.98.

items.q: A weak monobasic acid of concentration 0.1 mol/dm3 gives a hydrogen ion concentration of 0.002 mol/dm3. Calculate its acid dissociation constant.
A sparingly soluble salt of the type AB dissolves to give a solubility of 0.01 mol/dm3. Calculate its solubility product.
items.s: For AB, solubility product = s^2 = (0.01)^2 = 0.0001.

items.q: The solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt of the type AB is 0.0009. Calculate its solubility in mol/dm3.
items.s: For AB, solubility = sqrt(solubility product) = sqrt(0.0009) = 0.03 mol/dm3.

items.q: 25 cm3 of a solution of a strong monobasic acid required 22.7 cm3 of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.116 mol/dm3 for complete neutralisation. Calculate the concentration of the acid in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles of alkali = 0.116 x 22.7/1000; since the ratio is 1:1, acid concentration = 0.116 x 22.7/25 = 0.105 mol/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 aliquot of a metal ion solution required 27.4 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.026 mol/dm3. Given a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the amount of metal ion in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles of metal = millimoles of EDTA = 0.026 x 27.4 = 0.712 mmol.

items.q: A 100 cm3 sample of water required 20.6 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.012 mol/dm3. Taking the molar mass of calcium carbonate as 100 g/mol and a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the hardness in mg of calcium carbonate per dm3.
items.s: Moles of calcium = 0.012 x 20.6/1000 = 0.0002 mol in 100 cm3; mass of calcium carbonate = 0.0002 x 100 = 0.025 g, which in one dm3 is 247.2 mg/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 portion of an iron(II) solution required 25.9 cm3 of potassium permanganate solution of concentration 0.006 mol/dm3. One mole of permanganate oxidises five moles of iron(II). Calculate the amount of iron(II) in the portion in millimoles.
items.s: Moles of permanganate = 0.006 x 25.9/1000; iron(II) = 5 x that = 0.777 mmol.

items.q: A 25 cm3 sample of a solution of an oxidising agent required 27.4 cm3 of sodium thiosulphate solution of concentration 0.114 mol/dm3. One mole of the agent liberates 2 mol of iodine and one mole of iodine consumes two moles of thiosulphate. Calculate the concentration of the agent in mol/dm3.
items.s: Thiosulphate used = 0.114 x 27.4/1000 = 0.0031 mol; iodine = half of that; agent = iodine/2, so the concentration is 0.031 mol/dm3.

items.q: 0.985 g of an impure sample of a base of molar mass 56 g/mol was treated with 25 cm3 of hydrochloric acid of concentration 0.149 mol/dm3 and the excess acid required 7.8 cm3 of sodium hydroxide of concentration 0.042 mol/dm3. Taking the reaction ratio as 1:1 throughout, calculate the percentage purity of the sample.
items.s: Acid taken = 0.0037 mol; excess = 0.0003 mol; acid consumed = 0.0034 mol; mass of base = x 56 = 0.19 g, so purity = 19.32 per cent.

items.q: The standard potential of a metal electrode of the type M2+/M is 0.31 V. Calculate the electrode potential when the metal ion concentration is 0.01 mol/dm3, taking the term 2.303RT/nF as 0.0296 V.
items.s: For a divalent metal E = E0 + (0.0296) log[M2+] = 0.31 + 0.0296 x log(0.01) = 0.251 V.

items.q: A sample of mass 0.947 g gave a precipitate of mass 0.412 g whose gravimetric factor is 0.7. Calculate the percentage of the analyte in the sample.
items.s: Mass of analyte = 0.412 x 0.7 = 0.288 g; percentage = (0.288/0.947) x 100 = 30.45 per cent.

items.q: A sample of an ore of mass 0.989 g gave on ignition 0.437 g of Fe2O3 of molar mass 159.7 g/mol, which contains two atoms of iron of molar mass 55.85 g/mol. Calculate the percentage of iron in the ore.
items.s: The gravimetric factor is 2 x 55.85/159.7 = 0.699, so iron = 0.437 x 0.699 = 0.306 g and the percentage is 30.91.

items.q: Ignition of 1.02 g of a precipitate of molar mass 233.4 g/mol gave a weighable form that contains one atom of a metal of molar mass 137.3 g/mol. Calculate the mass of the metal in the precipitate, taking one mole of the metal per mole of the precipitate.
A conductivity cell of constant 2 cm-1 is filled with a solution whose conductance is 5.52 millisiemens. Calculate the conductivity in mS/cm.
items.s: Conductivity = conductance x cell constant = 5.52 x 2 = 11.04 mS/cm.

items.q: A solution of conductivity 3.81 mS/cm gives a conductance of 5.16 millisiemens in a conductivity cell. Calculate the cell constant in cm-1.
items.s: Cell constant = conductivity / conductance = 3.81 / 5.16 = 0.738 cm-1.

items.q: A glass electrode gives a potential that changes by 0.0592 V for each unit of pH. Calculate the change in potential in V when the pH of the solution changes from 4.2 to 7.2.
A solute has a retention time of 5.4 min on a column for which an unretained marker takes 1.34 min. Calculate the retention factor.
A peak with retention time 6.74 min has a base width of 0.84 min. Calculate the number of theoretical plates, using N = 16 (tR/w)^2.
Two peaks have retention times 9.17 min and 9.94 min and base widths 0.33 min and 0.51 min. Calculate the resolution.
Two solutes have retention factors of 0.9 and 1.8 on the same column. Calculate the selectivity factor.
items.s: Selectivity factor = k2/k1 = 1.8/0.9 = 2.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 50 cm3 containing a solute is shaken once with 50 cm3 of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 2. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase.
items.s: Fraction remaining = Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 50/(50 + 2 x 50) = 0.333.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 25 cm3 containing a solute is shaken twice, each time with a fresh 20 cm3 portion of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 3. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase after the two extractions.
items.s: Each extraction leaves Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 0.294, so after two the fraction is the square, 0.087.

items.q: A standard solution of concentration 0.0066 mol/dm3 gives a peak area of 0.352 and a sample gives a peak area of 0.465 under the same conditions. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.
items.s: Concentration is proportional to area, so c = 0.0066 x 0.465/0.352 = 0.0088 mol/dm3.

items.q: Five replicate titrations on the same solution gave the volumes 26.08, 25.94, 24.26, 26.76, 21.19 cm3. Calculate the mean titre in cm3.
items.s: Mean = sum of the five volumes divided by five = 24.85 cm3.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of copper in an alloy gave the percentages 13.56, 13.89, 14.37, 17.35, 19.47. Calculate the median percentage.
items.s: Arranged in order the values are 13.56, 13.89, 14.37, 17.35, 19.47, so the middle value is 14.37 per cent.

items.q: A solution transmits 47 per cent of the radiation at 520 nm. Calculate its absorbance.
A solution has an absorbance of 0.55 at 460 nm. Calculate the percentage of the incident radiation transmitted.
items.s: Transmittance = 10^(-A) x 100 = 10^(-0.55) x 100 = 28.18 per cent.

items.q: A volume of 100 cm3 of a solution that is 0.121 mol/dm3 in a compound of molar mass 58.5 g/mol is evaporated to dryness. Calculate the mass of residue in g.
A mass of 1.86 mg of an ion is present in 100 cm3 of solution. Calculate the concentration in parts per million, that is mg per dm3.
items.s: Concentration = 1.86 mg / (100/1000) dm3 = 18.6 ppm.

items.q: A titration required 26.6 cm3 of a titrant of concentration 0.056 mol/dm3. Calculate the amount of titrant used in moles.
items.s: Moles = concentration x volume in dm3 = 0.056 x 26.6/1000 = 0.0015 mol.

items.q: A 32 cm3 aliquot of a solution of concentration 0.11 mol/dm3 is taken. Calculate the amount of solute in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles = concentration x volume in cm3 = 0.11 x 32 = 3.52 mmol.

items.q: A solution of a strong monobasic acid has a hydrogen ion concentration of 0.002 mol/dm3. Calculate its pH.
A solution has a pH of 3.98. Calculate the hydrogen ion concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Hydrogen ion concentration = 10^(-pH) = 10^(-3.98) = 0.0001 mol/dm3.

items.q: A precipitate of mass 0.283 g was obtained whose gravimetric factor, converting the weighed form to the sought substance, is 0.25. Calculate the mass of the sought substance in g.
items.s: Mass sought = mass weighed x gravimetric factor = 0.283 x 0.25 = 0.071 g.

items.q: Which of the following best describes amperometry?
o: the reagent of known strength delivered from the burette during a volumetric determination
a technique in which the current at a fixed applied voltage is followed while reagent is added
a conducting path that joins two half cells while preventing their solutions from mixing
a membrane sensor whose potential changes with the hydrogen ion activity of the solution
items.s: amperometry: a technique in which the current at a fixed applied voltage is followed while reagent is added. The other options describe titrant, glass electrode, salt bridge.

items.q: Which of the following best describes titrant?
o: the reagent of known strength delivered from the burette during a volumetric determination
a measure of the spread of replicate results about their centre, obtained from the square root of the variance
the closeness of replicate results to one another
material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented
items.s: titrant: the reagent of known strength delivered from the burette during a volumetric determination. The other options describe precision, stratified portion, standard deviation.

items.q: confidence interval may be defined as
o: a measure of the spread of replicate results about their centre, obtained from the square root of the variance
the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity
a result that lies so far from the others that it is suspected of belonging to a different population
a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability
items.s: confidence interval: a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability. The other options describe standard deviation, outlier, cell constant.

items.q: The statement “the quantity of solute in grams present in one cubic decimetre of solution” describes which of the following?
o: mass concentration
molality
molarity
parts per million
items.s: mass concentration is the quantity of solute in grams present in one cubic decimetre of solution.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines equivalent weight?
o: a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
the closeness of replicate results to one another
the mass of a substance that supplies or consumes one mole of reacting units such as hydrogen ions or electrons
the wavelength at which two interconvertible species have equal absorptivity so absorbance does not change with their ratio
items.s: equivalent weight: the mass of a substance that supplies or consumes one mole of reacting units such as hydrogen ions or electrons. The other options describe precision, masking agent, isosbestic point.

items.q: Which term is described by “the closeness of replicate results to one another”?
o: systematic error
precision
accuracy
standard deviation
items.s: precision is the closeness of replicate results to one another.

items.q: Which term is described by “the scatter of replicate results expressed as a fraction of their centre value and often quoted as a percentage”?
o: accuracy
random error
precision
relative spread
items.s: relative spread is the scatter of replicate results expressed as a fraction of their centre value and often quoted as a percentage.

items.q: Which term is described by “the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part”?
o: amperometry
Nernst equation
conductivity
reference electrode
items.s: Nernst equation is the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines cell constant?
o: the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted
a bias that shifts every result in the same direction by a similar amount
the quotient of the total amount concentration of a solute in the organic phase to that in the aqueous phase at equilibrium
the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity
items.s: cell constant: the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity. The other options describe distribution ratio, systematic error, gross sample.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines dissociation constant?
o: one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector
items.s: dissociation constant: the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base. The other options describe parts per million, precipitate, retention volume.

items.q: Which of the following best describes mother liquor?
o: a proton donor that is only partly ionised in aqueous solution, so an equilibrium mixture results
the solution remaining after a solid has been separated
the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component
a method in which iodine liberated by the analyte is measured with thiosulphate
items.s: mother liquor: the solution remaining after a solid has been separated. The other options describe retention time, weak acid, iodometric titration.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines composite sample.
o: the wavelength at which two interconvertible species have equal absorptivity so absorbance does not change with their ratio
a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out
the unwanted inclusion of soluble impurities in a solid as it forms
the part of a molecule responsible for the absorption of light in the visible or ultraviolet region
items.s: composite sample: a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out. The other options describe chromophore, coprecipitation, isosbestic point.

items.q: Which of the following best describes transmittance?
o: the fraction of the incident radiant power that passes through the sample
a proton donor that is only partly ionised in aqueous solution, so an equilibrium mixture results
unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
items.s: transmittance: the fraction of the incident radiant power that passes through the sample. The other options describe digestion, weak acid, random error.

items.q: Which of the following best describes quartering?
o: one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity
a hypothetical zone of the column in which one equilibration of solute between the phases is achieved
a reduction technique in which a flattened heap is divided into four parts and two opposite parts are retained
items.s: quartering: a reduction technique in which a flattened heap is divided into four parts and two opposite parts are retained. The other options describe theoretical plate, parts per million, cell constant.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines salt bridge?
o: the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
a conducting path that joins two half cells while preventing their solutions from mixing
a bias that shifts every result in the same direction by a similar amount
items.s: salt bridge: a conducting path that joins two half cells while preventing their solutions from mixing. The other options describe systematic error, complexometric titration, molarity.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ability of a solution to carry current, measured as the conductance of a cell of unit dimensions”?
o: Nernst equation
potentiometry
conductivity
cell constant
items.s: conductivity is the ability of a solution to carry current, measured as the conductance of a cell of unit dimensions.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines riffle splitter?
o: the re-dispersion of a coagulated solid into colloidal particles, often caused by washing
a device that divides a flowing stream of powder into two equal portions over and over
the loss of electrons by a species, which increases its charge number
a method in which the analyte is converted into a sparingly soluble or volatile product that is weighed
items.s: riffle splitter: a device that divides a flowing stream of powder into two equal portions over and over. The other options describe oxidation, peptisation, gravimetric analysis.

items.q: The statement “the loss of electrons by a species, which increases its charge number” describes which of the following?
o: iodometric titration
standard potential
oxidation
metal indicator
items.s: oxidation is the loss of electrons by a species, which increases its charge number.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines transmittance.
o: the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
the fraction of the incident radiant power that passes through the sample
the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material
items.s: transmittance: the fraction of the incident radiant power that passes through the sample. The other options describe complexometric titration, molarity, laboratory sample.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines end point.
o: the stage at which the indicator changes colour, which is intended to coincide with complete reaction
a hypothetical zone of the column in which one equilibration of solute between the phases is achieved
material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented
a dye that binds the cation under determination and gives up its colour once the titrant has taken that cation away
items.s: end point: the stage at which the indicator changes colour, which is intended to coincide with complete reaction. The other options describe theoretical plate, metal indicator, stratified portion.

items.q: strong acid may be defined as
o: a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution
the gain of electrons by a species, accompanied by a fall in its oxidation number
the unwanted inclusion of soluble impurities in a solid as it forms
the negative logarithm to base ten of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
items.s: strong acid: a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution. The other options describe reduction, coprecipitation, pH.

items.q: Which term is described by “a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts”?
o: monochromator
calibration curve
cuvette
Beer-Lambert law
items.s: calibration curve is a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts.

items.q: outlier may be defined as
o: the ratio of the time a component spends in the fixed bed to the time it spends in the moving fluid
a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts
a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source
a result that lies so far from the others that it is suspected of belonging to a different population
items.s: outlier: a result that lies so far from the others that it is suspected of belonging to a different population. The other options describe retention factor, calibration curve, monochromator.

items.q: The statement “the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity” describes which of the following?
o: amperometry
reference electrode
cell constant
glass electrode
items.s: cell constant is the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity.

items.q: The statement “the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector” describes which of the following?
o: retention volume
retention factor
retention time
solvent extraction
items.s: retention volume is the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines confidence interval?
o: a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability
unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition
a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts
items.s: confidence interval: a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability. The other options describe random error, calibration curve, masking agent.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines gravimetric analysis?
o: the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet
a device that divides a flowing stream of powder into two equal portions over and over
a method in which the analyte is converted into a sparingly soluble or volatile product that is weighed
the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component
items.s: gravimetric analysis: a method in which the analyte is converted into a sparingly soluble or volatile product that is weighed. The other options describe riffle splitter, junction potential, retention time.

items.q: Which of the following best describes composite sample?
o: the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity
a measure of the spread of replicate results about their centre, obtained from the square root of the variance
the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity determined
a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out
items.s: composite sample: a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out. The other options describe accuracy, standard deviation, cell constant.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines isosbestic point?
o: a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
the wavelength at which two interconvertible species have equal absorptivity so absorbance does not change with their ratio
the fraction of the incident radiant power that passes through the sample
items.s: isosbestic point: the wavelength at which two interconvertible species have equal absorptivity so absorbance does not change with their ratio. The other options describe indicator, dissociation constant, transmittance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines buffer capacity.
o: the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably
material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented
the solution remaining after a solid has been separated
a membrane sensor whose potential changes with the hydrogen ion activity of the solution
items.s: buffer capacity: the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably. The other options describe mother liquor, glass electrode, stratified portion.

items.q: Which term is described by “the statement that absorbance is proportional to concentration and to the length of the light path”?
o: molar absorptivity
isosbestic point
monochromator
Beer-Lambert law
items.s: Beer-Lambert law is the statement that absorbance is proportional to concentration and to the length of the light path.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines monochromator.
o: the unwanted inclusion of soluble impurities in a solid as it forms
the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present
a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source
the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material
items.s: monochromator: a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source. The other options describe laboratory sample, equivalence point, coprecipitation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines systematic error?
o: the sum of the replicate results divided by the number of results
a bias that shifts every result in the same direction by a similar amount
the transfer of a solute from one liquid phase to another immiscible liquid
a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
items.s: systematic error: a bias that shifts every result in the same direction by a similar amount. The other options describe masking agent, solvent extraction, arithmetic mean.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines potentiometry?
o: the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet
unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition
items.s: potentiometry: the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution. The other options describe dissociation constant, junction potential, random error.

items.q: Which term is described by “a small portion withdrawn at one point in space or time while material is being collected”?
o: laboratory sample
stratified portion
increment
drying to constant mass
items.s: increment is a small portion withdrawn at one point in space or time while material is being collected.

items.q: The statement “the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present” describes which of the following?
o: equivalence point
dissociation constant
end point
buffer capacity
items.s: equivalence point is the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines outlier?
o: a result that lies so far from the others that it is suspected of belonging to a different population
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts
the stage at which the indicator changes colour, which is intended to coincide with complete reaction
items.s: outlier: a result that lies so far from the others that it is suspected of belonging to a different population. The other options describe end point, calibration curve, digestion.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines molarity.
o: an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance
the separation between two neighbouring peaks expressed in terms of their retention times and widths
the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution
items.s: molarity: the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution. The other options describe drying to constant mass, resolution, precipitate.

items.q: Which term is described by “the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted”?
o: representative portion
gross sample
composite sample
stratified portion
items.s: gross sample is the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted.

items.q: The statement “a conducting path that joins two half cells while preventing their solutions from mixing” describes which of the following?
o: glass electrode
salt bridge
Nernst equation
potentiometry
items.s: salt bridge is a conducting path that joins two half cells while preventing their solutions from mixing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines retention time?
o: the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component
the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity determined
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
items.s: retention time: the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component. The other options describe complexometric titration, accuracy, digestion.

items.q: Which term is described by “a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges”?
o: end point
equivalence point
strong acid
indicator
items.s: indicator is a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges.

items.q: composite sample may be defined as
o: the negative logarithm to base ten of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out
the absorbance of a solution of unit amount concentration measured in a cell of unit path length
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
items.s: composite sample: a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out. The other options describe pH, molar absorptivity, digestion.

items.q: Which term is described by “the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material”?
o: drying to constant mass
composite sample
representative portion
laboratory sample
items.s: laboratory sample is the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material.

items.q: Which term is described by “the gain of electrons by a species, accompanied by a fall in its oxidation number”?
o: ligand
conditional constant
reduction
masking agent
items.s: reduction is the gain of electrons by a species, accompanied by a fall in its oxidation number.

items.q: The statement “unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition” describes which of the following?
o: accuracy
random error
outlier
relative spread
items.s: random error is unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines gross sample.
o: material whose composition matches the bulk within the uncertainty required by the method
the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted
the gain of electrons by a species, accompanied by a fall in its oxidation number
the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet
items.s: gross sample: the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted. The other options describe representative portion, reduction, junction potential.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines molality?
o: a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
a membrane sensor whose potential changes with the hydrogen ion activity of the solution
the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent
the fixed material over which the moving fluid passes and with which components interact
items.s: molality: the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent. The other options describe masking agent, glass electrode, stationary phase.

items.q: All of the following belong to Chromatography and separation EXCEPT
o: equivalence point
chromatography
retention time
stationary phase
items.s: Every other option belongs to Chromatography and separation. “equivalence point” belongs to Acid-base equilibria and titration, not Chromatography and separation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines cuvette.
o: the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
a transparent cell of fixed path length that holds the solution in the light beam
a half cell of constant known voltage against which the sensing half cell is measured
items.s: cuvette: a transparent cell of fixed path length that holds the solution in the light beam. The other options describe Nernst equation, digestion, reference electrode.

items.q: Which term is described by “the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector”?
o: retention factor
retention volume
solvent extraction
theoretical plate
items.s: retention volume is the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector.

items.q: Which term is described by “a transparent cell of fixed path length that holds the solution in the light beam”?
o: transmittance
molar absorptivity
monochromator
cuvette
items.s: cuvette is a transparent cell of fixed path length that holds the solution in the light beam.

items.q: Which term is described by “the logarithm to base ten of the ratio of incident to transmitted radiant power”?
o: monochromator
absorbance
molar absorptivity
chromophore
items.s: absorbance is the logarithm to base ten of the ratio of incident to transmitted radiant power.

items.q: The statement “a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts” describes which of the following?
o: isosbestic point
transmittance
calibration curve
monochromator
items.s: calibration curve is a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts.

items.q: Which term is described by “a measure of the spread of replicate results about their centre, obtained from the square root of the variance”?
o: accuracy
confidence interval
standard deviation
random error
items.s: standard deviation is a measure of the spread of replicate results about their centre, obtained from the square root of the variance.

items.q: The statement “material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented” describes which of the following?
o: representative portion
composite sample
quartering
stratified portion
items.s: stratified portion is material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented.

items.q: Which of the following best describes molality?
o: a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution
the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent
the ratio of the molar mass of the sought substance to that of the weighed form, allowing for stoichiometry
a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability
items.s: molality: the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent. The other options describe gravimetric factor, strong acid, confidence interval.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines potentiometry.
o: the closeness of replicate results to one another
the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector
heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance
the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution
items.s: potentiometry: the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution. The other options describe drying to constant mass, retention volume, precision.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines retention time.
o: the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component
the ratio of the molar mass of the sought substance to that of the weighed form, allowing for stoichiometry
the transfer of a solute from one liquid phase to another immiscible liquid
a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source
items.s: retention time: the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component. The other options describe gravimetric factor, monochromator, solvent extraction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes monochromator?
o: a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source
the electrode voltage of a half reaction measured with every species held at unit activity
the loss of electrons by a species, which increases its charge number
the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted
items.s: monochromator: a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source. The other options describe gross sample, oxidation, standard potential.

items.q: Which of the following best describes dissociation constant?
o: the ability of a solution to carry current, measured as the conductance of a cell of unit dimensions
the closeness of replicate results to one another
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
the ratio of the time a component spends in the fixed bed to the time it spends in the moving fluid
items.s: dissociation constant: the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base. The other options describe conductivity, retention factor, precision.

items.q: Which term is described by “an ion or molecule that donates an electron pair to a central metal to form a coordination compound”?
o: masking agent
complexometric titration
ligand
oxidation
items.s: ligand is an ion or molecule that donates an electron pair to a central metal to form a coordination compound.

items.q: resolution may be defined as
o: a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability
an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
the separation between two neighbouring peaks expressed in terms of their retention times and widths
the fraction of the incident radiant power that passes through the sample
items.s: resolution: the separation between two neighbouring peaks expressed in terms of their retention times and widths. The other options describe precipitate, transmittance, confidence interval.

items.q: Which term is described by “an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction”?
o: coprecipitation
peptisation
precipitate
ignition
items.s: precipitate is an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines reference electrode.
o: the absorbance of a solution of unit amount concentration measured in a cell of unit path length
the stage at which the indicator changes colour, which is intended to coincide with complete reaction
material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented
a half cell of constant known voltage against which the sensing half cell is measured
items.s: reference electrode: a half cell of constant known voltage against which the sensing half cell is measured. The other options describe end point, stratified portion, molar absorptivity.

items.q: Six replicate measurements of a titre gave a mean of 33 cm3 and a standard deviation of 0.57 cm3. Calculate the relative spread of the results in per cent.
items.s: Relative spread = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (0.57/33) x 100 = 1.73 per cent.

items.q: A solution is 0.0005 mol/dm3 in a coloured species whose molar absorptivity is 3465 dm3 mol-1 cm-1; the absorbance was measured in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the absorbance.
items.s: A = absorptivity x concentration x path length = 3465 x 0.0005 x 1.00 = 1.8.

items.q: A mass of 2.37 g of a compound of molar mass 98 g/mol is dissolved in water and made up to 500 cm3. Calculate the molar concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles = 2.37/98 = 0.024; concentration = moles/(500/1000) = 0.048 mol/dm3.

items.q: 50 cm3 of a solution of concentration 0.784 mol/dm3 is diluted with water to a final volume of 500 cm3. Calculate the concentration of the diluted solution in mol/dm3.
A buffer is made from a weak acid of pKa 7.25 and its sodium salt, the ratio of salt concentration to acid concentration being 3. Calculate the pH of the buffer.
items.s: pH = pKa + log(salt/acid) = 7.25 + log(3) = 7.73.

items.q: A sparingly soluble salt of the type AB dissolves to give a solubility of 0.02 mol/dm3. Calculate its solubility product.
items.s: For AB, solubility product = s^2 = (0.02)^2 = 0.0004.

items.q: 25 cm3 of a solution of a strong monobasic acid required 21.9 cm3 of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.142 mol/dm3 for complete neutralisation. Calculate the concentration of the acid in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles of alkali = 0.142 x 21.9/1000; since the ratio is 1:1, acid concentration = 0.142 x 21.9/25 = 0.124 mol/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 aliquot of a metal ion solution required 30.7 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.012 mol/dm3. Given a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the amount of metal ion in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles of metal = millimoles of EDTA = 0.012 x 30.7 = 0.368 mmol.

items.q: The standard potential of a metal electrode of the type M2+/M is 0.66 V. Calculate the electrode potential when the metal ion concentration is 0.005 mol/dm3, taking the term 2.303RT/nF as 0.0296 V.
items.s: For a divalent metal E = E0 + (0.0296) log[M2+] = 0.66 + 0.0296 x log(0.005) = 0.592 V.

items.q: A sample of mass 1 g gave a precipitate of mass 0.206 g whose gravimetric factor is 0.3. Calculate the percentage of the analyte in the sample.
items.s: Mass of analyte = 0.206 x 0.3 = 0.062 g; percentage = (0.062/1) x 100 = 6.18 per cent.

items.q: A conductivity cell of constant 1.2 cm-1 is filled with a solution whose conductance is 6.95 millisiemens. Calculate the conductivity in mS/cm.
items.s: Conductivity = conductance x cell constant = 6.95 x 1.2 = 8.34 mS/cm.

items.q: A solute has a retention time of 3.91 min on a column for which an unretained marker takes 0.63 min. Calculate the retention factor.
Two solutes have retention factors of 2.34 and 3.51 on the same column. Calculate the selectivity factor.
items.s: Selectivity factor = k2/k1 = 3.51/2.34 = 1.5.

items.q: Five replicate titrations on the same solution gave the volumes 25.41, 23.57, 29.73, 21.89, 27.47 cm3. Calculate the mean titre in cm3.
items.s: Mean = sum of the five volumes divided by five = 25.61 cm3.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of copper in an alloy gave the percentages 13.56, 17.72, 17.76, 18.77, 19.39. Calculate the median percentage.
items.s: Arranged in order the values are 13.56, 17.72, 17.76, 18.77, 19.39, so the middle value is 17.76 per cent.

items.q: A mean of 25 mg was obtained from 5 replicate determinations whose standard deviation was 0.61 mg. Taking the Student t value for the stated degrees of freedom as 2.57, calculate the half width of the 95 per cent confidence interval in mg.
items.s: Half width = t x standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 2.57 x 0.61 / sqrt(5) = 0.701 mg.

items.q: Four replicate results arranged in ascending order are 22, 29, 31 and 39. The first result is suspected of being an outlier. Using Q = gap / spread, calculate the rejection quotient.
items.s: Q = (second value - first value)/(largest - smallest) = (29 - 22)/(39 - 22) = 0.412.

items.q: The mean of 5 replicate determinations is 21.71 mg and their standard deviation is 1.07 mg, while the certified value for the material is 21.27 mg. Calculate the value of t.
items.s: t = |mean - certified| x sqrt(n) / standard deviation = 0.44 x sqrt(5) / 1.07 = 0.92.

items.q: The result of a determination is calculated as the product of two measured quantities whose relative uncertainties are 2 per cent and 2.1 per cent. Calculate the relative uncertainty of the result in per cent.
items.s: For a product the relative uncertainties combine in quadrature: sqrt(2^2 + 2.1^2) = 2.9 per cent.

items.q: A solution transmits 25 per cent of the radiation at 520 nm. Calculate its absorbance.
A solution has an absorbance of 1.38 at 460 nm. Calculate the percentage of the incident radiation transmitted.
items.s: Transmittance = 10^(-A) x 100 = 10^(-1.38) x 100 = 4.17 per cent.

items.q: A solution of a species whose molar absorptivity is 4390 dm3 mol-1 cm-1 gives an absorbance of 0.93 in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: c = A / (absorptivity x path length) = 0.93 / (4390 x 1.00) = 0.0002 mol/dm3.

items.q: A solution of concentration 0.0006 mol/dm3 gives an absorbance of 0.318 in a cell of path length 1 cm. Calculate the molar absorptivity in dm3 mol-1 cm-1.
items.s: Absorptivity = A / (c x b) = 0.318 / (0.0006 x 1) = 504.8 dm3 mol-1 cm-1.

items.q: A calibration line of absorbance against concentration passes through the standard points (0.002 mol/dm3, 0.264) and (0.01 mol/dm3, 1.1). A sample gives an absorbance of 0.68. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.
A volume of 226 cm3 of a solution that is 0.186 mol/dm3 in a compound of molar mass 106 g/mol is evaporated to dryness. Calculate the mass of residue in g.
A mass of 2.95 mg of an ion is present in 250 cm3 of solution. Calculate the concentration in parts per million, that is mg per dm3.
items.s: Concentration = 2.95 mg / (250/1000) dm3 = 11.8 ppm.

items.q: A standard solution of concentration 0.079 mol/dm3 is to be prepared in a 100 cm3 volumetric flask from a solid of molar mass 106 g/mol. Calculate the mass of solid required in g.
A titration required 27.5 cm3 of a titrant of concentration 0.079 mol/dm3. Calculate the amount of titrant used in moles.
items.s: Moles = concentration x volume in dm3 = 0.079 x 27.5/1000 = 0.0022 mol.

items.q: A 37 cm3 aliquot of a solution of concentration 0.243 mol/dm3 is taken. Calculate the amount of solute in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles = concentration x volume in cm3 = 0.243 x 37 = 8.99 mmol.

items.q: A solution of a strong monobasic acid has a hydrogen ion concentration of 0.01 mol/dm3. Calculate its pH.
A solution has a pH of 3.65. Calculate the hydrogen ion concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Hydrogen ion concentration = 10^(-pH) = 10^(-3.65) = 0.0002 mol/dm3.

items.q: A buffer of pH 4.71 is required from a weak acid of pKa 5.01. Calculate the ratio of the concentration of the conjugate base to that of the acid.
items.s: From pH = pKa + log(ratio), log(ratio) = 4.71 - 5.01, so the ratio is 0.501.

items.q: A weak monobasic acid of concentration 0.05 mol/dm3 gives a hydrogen ion concentration of 0.0005 mol/dm3. Calculate its acid dissociation constant.
The solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt of the type AB is 0.0001. Calculate its solubility in mol/dm3.
items.s: For AB, solubility = sqrt(solubility product) = sqrt(0.0001) = 0.01 mol/dm3.

items.q: A 50 cm3 sample of water required 13.4 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.015 mol/dm3. Taking the molar mass of calcium carbonate as 100 g/mol and a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the hardness in mg of calcium carbonate per dm3.
items.s: Moles of calcium = 0.015 x 13.4/1000 = 0.0002 mol in 50 cm3; mass of calcium carbonate = 0.0002 x 100 = 0.02 g, which in one dm3 is 402 mg/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 portion of an iron(II) solution required 21.8 cm3 of potassium permanganate solution of concentration 0.006 mol/dm3. One mole of permanganate oxidises five moles of iron(II). Calculate the amount of iron(II) in the portion in millimoles.
items.s: Moles of permanganate = 0.006 x 21.8/1000; iron(II) = 5 x that = 0.654 mmol.

items.q: A 50 cm3 sample of a solution of an oxidising agent required 27 cm3 of sodium thiosulphate solution of concentration 0.077 mol/dm3. One mole of the agent liberates 1 mol of iodine and one mole of iodine consumes two moles of thiosulphate. Calculate the concentration of the agent in mol/dm3.
items.s: Thiosulphate used = 0.077 x 27/1000 = 0.0021 mol; iodine = half of that; agent = iodine/1, so the concentration is 0.021 mol/dm3.

items.q: 0.823 g of an impure sample of a base of molar mass 61 g/mol was treated with 25 cm3 of hydrochloric acid of concentration 0.133 mol/dm3 and the excess acid required 7.8 cm3 of sodium hydroxide of concentration 0.082 mol/dm3. Taking the reaction ratio as 1:1 throughout, calculate the percentage purity of the sample.
items.s: Acid taken = 0.0033 mol; excess = 0.0006 mol; acid consumed = 0.0027 mol; mass of base = x 61 = 0.164 g, so purity = 19.9 per cent.

items.q: A sample of an ore of mass 1.96 g gave on ignition 0.76 g of Fe2O3 of molar mass 159.7 g/mol, which contains two atoms of iron of molar mass 55.85 g/mol. Calculate the percentage of iron in the ore.
items.s: The gravimetric factor is 2 x 55.85/159.7 = 0.699, so iron = 0.76 x 0.699 = 0.532 g and the percentage is 27.12.

items.q: A precipitate of mass 0.664 g was obtained whose gravimetric factor, converting the weighed form to the sought substance, is 0.25. Calculate the mass of the sought substance in g.
items.s: Mass sought = mass weighed x gravimetric factor = 0.664 x 0.25 = 0.166 g.

items.q: Ignition of 0.308 g of a precipitate of molar mass 159.7 g/mol gave a weighable form that contains one atom of a metal of molar mass 63.5 g/mol. Calculate the mass of the metal in the precipitate, taking one mole of the metal per mole of the precipitate.
A solution of conductivity 8.28 mS/cm gives a conductance of 5.94 millisiemens in a conductivity cell. Calculate the cell constant in cm-1.
items.s: Cell constant = conductivity / conductance = 8.28 / 5.94 = 1.39 cm-1.

items.q: Two half cells have standard potentials of -0.29 V and -0.03 V. Calculate the standard cell potential obtained by coupling them.
items.s: The couple with the higher potential acts as the cathode, so the cell potential is -0.03 - (-0.29) = 0.26 V.

items.q: A peak with retention time 4.59 min has a base width of 0.31 min. Calculate the number of theoretical plates, using N = 16 (tR/w)^2.
Two peaks have retention times 10.47 min and 11.6 min and base widths 0.5 min and 0.56 min. Calculate the resolution.

An aqueous solution of volume 50 cm3 containing a solute is shaken once with 20 cm3 of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 12. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase.
items.s: Fraction remaining = Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 50/(50 + 12 x 20) = 0.172.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 100 cm3 containing a solute is shaken twice, each time with a fresh 25 cm3 portion of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 9. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase after the two extractions.
items.s: Each extraction leaves Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 0.308, so after two the fraction is the square, 0.095.

items.q: A standard solution of concentration 0.0064 mol/dm3 gives a peak area of 0.782 and a sample gives a peak area of 0.88 under the same conditions. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.
items.s: Concentration is proportional to area, so c = 0.0064 x 0.88/0.782 = 0.0072 mol/dm3.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of iron in an ore gave the percentages 13.6, 10.78, 15.62, 17.98, 17.59. Calculate the standard deviation of the results in per cent.
items.s: The mean is 15.11; the sum of squared deviations is 35.68; dividing by four and taking the root gives 2.99 per cent.

items.q: Six replicate measurements of a titre gave a mean of 39 cm3 and a standard deviation of 1.57 cm3. Calculate the relative spread of the results in per cent.
items.s: Relative spread = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (1.57/39) x 100 = 4.03 per cent.

items.q: A solution is 0.0002 mol/dm3 in a coloured species whose molar absorptivity is 3280 dm3 mol-1 cm-1; the absorbance was measured in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the absorbance.
items.s: A = absorptivity x concentration x path length = 3280 x 0.0002 x 1.00 = 0.656.

items.q: A mass of 4.85 g of a compound of molar mass 84 g/mol is dissolved in water and made up to 1000 cm3. Calculate the molar concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles = 4.85/84 = 0.058; concentration = moles/(1000/1000) = 0.058 mol/dm3.

items.q: 33 cm3 of a solution of concentration 0.798 mol/dm3 is diluted with water to a final volume of 500 cm3. Calculate the concentration of the diluted solution in mol/dm3.
A buffer is made from a weak acid of pKa 6.55 and its sodium salt, the ratio of salt concentration to acid concentration being 1. Calculate the pH of the buffer.
items.s: pH = pKa + log(salt/acid) = 6.55 + log(1) = 6.55.

items.q: 25 cm3 of a solution of a strong monobasic acid required 19 cm3 of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.158 mol/dm3 for complete neutralisation. Calculate the concentration of the acid in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles of alkali = 0.158 x 19/1000; since the ratio is 1:1, acid concentration = 0.158 x 19/25 = 0.12 mol/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 aliquot of a metal ion solution required 19.7 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.007 mol/dm3. Given a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the amount of metal ion in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles of metal = millimoles of EDTA = 0.007 x 19.7 = 0.138 mmol.

items.q: The standard potential of a metal electrode of the type M2+/M is 0.39 V. Calculate the electrode potential when the metal ion concentration is 0.1 mol/dm3, taking the term 2.303RT/nF as 0.0296 V.
items.s: For a divalent metal E = E0 + (0.0296) log[M2+] = 0.39 + 0.0296 x log(0.1) = 0.36 V.

items.q: A sample of mass 0.731 g gave a precipitate of mass 0.306 g whose gravimetric factor is 0.3. Calculate the percentage of the analyte in the sample.
items.s: Mass of analyte = 0.306 x 0.3 = 0.092 g; percentage = (0.092/0.731) x 100 = 12.56 per cent.

items.q: A conductivity cell of constant 1.2 cm-1 is filled with a solution whose conductance is 2.09 millisiemens. Calculate the conductivity in mS/cm.
items.s: Conductivity = conductance x cell constant = 2.09 x 1.2 = 2.51 mS/cm.

items.q: A glass electrode gives a potential that changes by 0.0592 V for each unit of pH. Calculate the change in potential in V when the pH of the solution changes from 3.9 to 4.9.
Choose the option that explains what normality means.
o: the number of equivalent weights of solute present in one cubic decimetre of solution
one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the reagent of known strength delivered from the burette during a volumetric determination
a highly pure stable substance weighed directly to prepare a solution of known strength
items.s: normality: the number of equivalent weights of solute present in one cubic decimetre of solution. The other options describe parts per million, titrant, primary standard.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges”
o: strong acid
equivalence point
dissociation constant
indicator
items.s: indicator is a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what metal indicator means.
o: a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
a dye that binds the cation under determination and gives up its colour once the titrant has taken that cation away

items.s: Moles of permanganate = 0.028 x 28/1000; iron(II) = 5 x that = 3.92 mmol.

items.s: The gravimetric factor is 2 x 55.85/159.7 = 0.699, so iron = 0.434 x 0.699 = 0.304 g and the percentage is 27.6.

A solution of conductivity 4.65 mS/cm gives a conductance of 5.83 millisiemens in a conductivity cell. Calculate the cell constant in cm-1.

items.s: Relative spread = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (0.65/27) x 100 = 2.41 per cent.

items.q: The mean of 9 replicate determinations is 22.77 mg and their standard deviation is 0.69 mg, while the certified value for the material is 22.38 mg. Calculate the value of t.
items.s: t = |mean - certified| x sqrt(n) / standard deviation = 0.39 x sqrt(9) / 0.69 = 1.7.

items.q: The result of a determination is calculated as the product of two measured quantities whose relative uncertainties are 2.4 per cent and 2 per cent. Calculate the relative uncertainty of the result in per cent.
items.s: For a product the relative uncertainties combine in quadrature: sqrt(2.4^2 + 2^2) = 3.12 per cent.

items.q: A solution transmits 73 per cent of the radiation at 520 nm. Calculate its absorbance.
A solution has an absorbance of 0.84 at 460 nm. Calculate the percentage of the incident radiation transmitted.
items.s: Transmittance = 10^(-A) x 100 = 10^(-0.84) x 100 = 14.45 per cent.

items.q: A solution is 0.0005 mol/dm3 in a coloured species whose molar absorptivity is 2485 dm3 mol-1 cm-1; the absorbance was measured in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the absorbance.
items.s: A = absorptivity x concentration x path length = 2485 x 0.0005 x 1.00 = 1.32.

items.q: A calibration line of absorbance against concentration passes through the standard points (0.002 mol/dm3, 0.317) and (0.01 mol/dm3, 1.05). A sample gives an absorbance of 0.609. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.
A volume of 191 cm3 of a solution that is 0.051 mol/dm3 in a compound of molar mass 40 g/mol is evaporated to dryness. Calculate the mass of residue in g.
A mass of 2.71 g of a compound of molar mass 40 g/mol is dissolved in water and made up to 250 cm3. Calculate the molar concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles = 2.71/40 = 0.068; concentration = moles/(250/1000) = 0.271 mol/dm3.

items.q: 20 cm3 of a solution of concentration 0.444 mol/dm3 is diluted with water to a final volume of 250 cm3. Calculate the concentration of the diluted solution in mol/dm3.
A mass of 11.27 mg of an ion is present in 50 cm3 of solution. Calculate the concentration in parts per million, that is mg per dm3.
items.s: Concentration = 11.27 mg / (50/1000) dm3 = 225.4 ppm.

items.q: A titration required 26 cm3 of a titrant of concentration 0.23 mol/dm3. Calculate the amount of titrant used in moles.
items.s: Moles = concentration x volume in dm3 = 0.23 x 26/1000 = 0.006 mol.

items.q: A 46 cm3 aliquot of a solution of concentration 0.287 mol/dm3 is taken. Calculate the amount of solute in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles = concentration x volume in cm3 = 0.287 x 46 = 13.2 mmol.

items.q: A solution of a strong monobasic acid has a hydrogen ion concentration of 0.001 mol/dm3. Calculate its pH.
A solution has a pH of 3.96. Calculate the hydrogen ion concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Hydrogen ion concentration = 10^(-pH) = 10^(-3.96) = 0.0001 mol/dm3.

items.q: A buffer is made from a weak acid of pKa 5 and its sodium salt, the ratio of salt concentration to acid concentration being 0.5. Calculate the pH of the buffer.
items.s: pH = pKa + log(salt/acid) = 5 + log(0.5) = 4.7.

items.q: A sparingly soluble salt of the type AB dissolves to give a solubility of 0.05 mol/dm3. Calculate its solubility product.
items.s: For AB, solubility product = s^2 = (0.05)^2 = 0.0025.

items.q: 25 cm3 of a solution of a strong monobasic acid required 22.4 cm3 of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.061 mol/dm3 for complete neutralisation. Calculate the concentration of the acid in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles of alkali = 0.061 x 22.4/1000; since the ratio is 1:1, acid concentration = 0.061 x 22.4/25 = 0.055 mol/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 aliquot of a metal ion solution required 26.6 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.016 mol/dm3. Given a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the amount of metal ion in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles of metal = millimoles of EDTA = 0.016 x 26.6 = 0.426 mmol.

items.q: A 50 cm3 sample of a solution of an oxidising agent required 11.8 cm3 of sodium thiosulphate solution of concentration 0.117 mol/dm3. One mole of the agent liberates 1 mol of iodine and one mole of iodine consumes two moles of thiosulphate. Calculate the concentration of the agent in mol/dm3.
items.s: Thiosulphate used = 0.117 x 11.8/1000 = 0.0014 mol; iodine = half of that; agent = iodine/1, so the concentration is 0.014 mol/dm3.

items.q: 0.759 g of an impure sample of a base of molar mass 61 g/mol was treated with 50 cm3 of hydrochloric acid of concentration 0.092 mol/dm3 and the excess acid required 14.7 cm3 of sodium hydroxide of concentration 0.034 mol/dm3. Taking the reaction ratio as 1:1 throughout, calculate the percentage purity of the sample.
items.s: Acid taken = 0.0046 mol; excess = 0.0005 mol; acid consumed = 0.0041 mol; mass of base = x 61 = 0.25 g, so purity = 32.95 per cent.

items.q: The standard potential of a metal electrode of the type M2+/M is 0.15 V. Calculate the electrode potential when the metal ion concentration is 0.005 mol/dm3, taking the term 2.303RT/nF as 0.0296 V.
items.s: For a divalent metal E = E0 + (0.0296) log[M2+] = 0.15 + 0.0296 x log(0.005) = 0.082 V.

items.q: A sample of mass 1.16 g gave a precipitate of mass 0.229 g whose gravimetric factor is 0.7. Calculate the percentage of the analyte in the sample.
items.s: Mass of analyte = 0.229 x 0.7 = 0.16 g; percentage = (0.16/1.16) x 100 = 13.82 per cent.

items.q: A precipitate of mass 0.752 g was obtained whose gravimetric factor, converting the weighed form to the sought substance, is 0.25. Calculate the mass of the sought substance in g.
items.s: Mass sought = mass weighed x gravimetric factor = 0.752 x 0.25 = 0.188 g.

items.q: A conductivity cell of constant 1.2 cm-1 is filled with a solution whose conductance is 5.7 millisiemens. Calculate the conductivity in mS/cm.
items.s: Conductivity = conductance x cell constant = 5.7 x 1.2 = 6.84 mS/cm.

items.q: Two half cells have standard potentials of 0.24 V and -0.42 V. Calculate the standard cell potential obtained by coupling them.
items.s: The couple with the higher potential acts as the cathode, so the cell potential is 0.24 - (-0.42) = 0.66 V.

items.q: A glass electrode gives a potential that changes by 0.0592 V for each unit of pH. Calculate the change in potential in V when the pH of the solution changes from 4.4 to 7.4.
A solute has a retention time of 10.17 min on a column for which an unretained marker takes 1.96 min. Calculate the retention factor.
Two solutes have retention factors of 1.97 and 2.96 on the same column. Calculate the selectivity factor.
items.s: Selectivity factor = k2/k1 = 2.96/1.97 = 1.5.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 25 cm3 containing a solute is shaken once with 10 cm3 of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 5. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase.
items.s: Fraction remaining = Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 25/(25 + 5 x 10) = 0.333.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 25 cm3 containing a solute is shaken twice, each time with a fresh 20 cm3 portion of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 9. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase after the two extractions.
items.s: Each extraction leaves Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 0.122, so after two the fraction is the square, 0.015.

items.q: A mean of 24 mg was obtained from 4 replicate determinations whose standard deviation was 0.7 mg. Taking the Student t value for the stated degrees of freedom as 2.26, calculate the half width of the 95 per cent confidence interval in mg.
items.s: Half width = t x standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 2.26 x 0.7 / sqrt(4) = 0.791 mg.

items.q: Four replicate results arranged in ascending order are 22, 30, 32 and 34. The first result is suspected of being an outlier. Using Q = gap / spread, calculate the rejection quotient.
items.s: Q = (second value - first value)/(largest - smallest) = (30 - 22)/(34 - 22) = 0.667.

items.q: A solution of a species whose molar absorptivity is 4181 dm3 mol-1 cm-1 gives an absorbance of 0.902 in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: c = A / (absorptivity x path length) = 0.902 / (4181 x 1.00) = 0.0002 mol/dm3.

items.q: A solution of concentration 0.0006 mol/dm3 gives an absorbance of 0.529 in a cell of path length 2 cm. Calculate the molar absorptivity in dm3 mol-1 cm-1.
items.s: Absorptivity = A / (c x b) = 0.529 / (0.0006 x 2) = 426.6 dm3 mol-1 cm-1.

items.q: A standard solution of concentration 0.13 mol/dm3 is to be prepared in a 100 cm3 volumetric flask from a solid of molar mass 84 g/mol. Calculate the mass of solid required in g.
A buffer of pH 5.84 is required from a weak acid of pKa 6.14. Calculate the ratio of the concentration of the conjugate base to that of the acid.
items.s: From pH = pKa + log(ratio), log(ratio) = 5.84 - 6.14, so the ratio is 0.501.

items.q: The solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt of the type AB is 0.0025. Calculate its solubility in mol/dm3.
items.s: For AB, solubility = sqrt(solubility product) = sqrt(0.0025) = 0.05 mol/dm3.

items.q: A 50 cm3 sample of water required 20.4 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.01 mol/dm3. Taking the molar mass of calcium carbonate as 100 g/mol and a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the hardness in mg of calcium carbonate per dm3.
items.s: Moles of calcium = 0.01 x 20.4/1000 = 0.0002 mol in 50 cm3; mass of calcium carbonate = 0.0002 x 100 = 0.02 g, which in one dm3 is 408 mg/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 portion of an iron(II) solution required 22 cm3 of potassium permanganate solution of concentration 0.028 mol/dm3. One mole of permanganate oxidises five moles of iron(II). Calculate the amount of iron(II) in the portion in millimoles.
items.s: Moles of permanganate = 0.028 x 22/1000; iron(II) = 5 x that = 3.08 mmol.

items.q: A sample of an ore of mass 0.556 g gave on ignition 0.535 g of Fe2O3 of molar mass 159.7 g/mol, which contains two atoms of iron of molar mass 55.85 g/mol. Calculate the percentage of iron in the ore.
items.s: The gravimetric factor is 2 x 55.85/159.7 = 0.699, so iron = 0.535 x 0.699 = 0.374 g and the percentage is 67.3.

items.q: Ignition of 1.05 g of a precipitate of molar mass 233.4 g/mol gave a weighable form that contains one atom of a metal of molar mass 63.5 g/mol. Calculate the mass of the metal in the precipitate, taking one mole of the metal per mole of the precipitate.
A solution of conductivity 5.89 mS/cm gives a conductance of 4.25 millisiemens in a conductivity cell. Calculate the cell constant in cm-1.
items.s: Cell constant = conductivity / conductance = 5.89 / 4.25 = 1.39 cm-1.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines absorbance.
o: the wavelength at which two interconvertible species have equal absorptivity so absorbance does not change with their ratio
a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts
a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source
the logarithm to base ten of the ratio of incident to transmitted radiant power
items.s: absorbance: the logarithm to base ten of the ratio of incident to transmitted radiant power. The other options describe isosbestic point, calibration curve, monochromator.

items.q: solvent extraction is best described as
o: a hypothetical zone of the column in which one equilibration of solute between the phases is achieved
the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component
the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector
the transfer of a solute from one liquid phase to another immiscible liquid
items.s: solvent extraction: the transfer of a solute from one liquid phase to another immiscible liquid. The other options describe retention time, retention volume, theoretical plate.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Concentration units and standard solutions?
