normality
drying to constant mass
molarity
items.s: Every other option belongs to Concentration units and standard solutions. “drying to constant mass” belongs to Sampling and sample preparation, not Concentration units and standard solutions.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines ignition?
o: a method in which the analyte is converted into a sparingly soluble or volatile product that is weighed
the re-dispersion of a coagulated solid into colloidal particles, often caused by washing
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
strong heating of a solid to convert it into a stable weighable form
items.s: ignition: strong heating of a solid to convert it into a stable weighable form. The other options describe digestion, peptisation, gravimetric analysis.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones”
o: peptisation
digestion
coprecipitation
gravimetric analysis
items.s: digestion is keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones.

items.q: relative spread may be defined as
o: the scatter of replicate results expressed as a fraction of their centre value and often quoted as a percentage
a measure of the spread of replicate results about their centre, obtained from the square root of the variance
the closeness of replicate results to one another
a bias that shifts every result in the same direction by a similar amount
items.s: relative spread: the scatter of replicate results expressed as a fraction of their centre value and often quoted as a percentage. The other options describe precision, systematic error, standard deviation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines occlusion.
o: trapping of foreign ions inside the growing lattice of a solid
the solution remaining after a solid has been separated
a method in which the analyte is converted into a sparingly soluble or volatile product that is weighed
an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
items.s: occlusion: trapping of foreign ions inside the growing lattice of a solid. The other options describe gravimetric analysis, precipitate, mother liquor.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines normality.
o: the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution
the number of equivalent weights of solute present in one cubic decimetre of solution
one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the quantity of solute in grams present in one cubic decimetre of solution
items.s: normality: the number of equivalent weights of solute present in one cubic decimetre of solution. The other options describe mass concentration, parts per million, molarity.

items.q: buffer solution is best described as
o: a mixture that resists a change in hydrogen ion level when small amounts of acid or alkali are added
the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably
the negative logarithm to base ten of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present
items.s: buffer solution: a mixture that resists a change in hydrogen ion level when small amounts of acid or alkali are added. The other options describe pH, buffer capacity, equivalence point.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source”
o: molar absorptivity
calibration curve
cuvette
monochromator
items.s: monochromator is a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source.

items.q: Which of the following best describes precipitate?
o: an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
a method in which the analyte is converted into a sparingly soluble or volatile product that is weighed
the re-dispersion of a coagulated solid into colloidal particles, often caused by washing
strong heating of a solid to convert it into a stable weighable form
items.s: precipitate: an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction. The other options describe peptisation, ignition, gravimetric analysis.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution”
o: Nernst equation
junction potential
potentiometry
reference electrode
items.s: potentiometry is the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution.

items.q: conditional constant may be defined as
o: the effective stability quotient of a coordination compound at a stated acidity, allowing for side reactions
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
an ion or molecule that donates an electron pair to a central metal to form a coordination compound
items.s: conditional constant: the effective stability quotient of a coordination compound at a stated acidity, allowing for side reactions. The other options describe complexometric titration, masking agent, ligand.

items.q: Which term is described by “a measured portion taken from a larger volume for a single determination”?
o: normality
aliquot
molality
titrant
items.s: aliquot is a measured portion taken from a larger volume for a single determination.

items.q: Which term is described by “the absorbance of a solution of unit amount concentration measured in a cell of unit path length”?
o: absorbance
molar absorptivity
monochromator
calibration curve
items.s: molar absorptivity is the absorbance of a solution of unit amount concentration measured in a cell of unit path length.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines mother liquor.
o: strong heating of a solid to convert it into a stable weighable form
the re-dispersion of a coagulated solid into colloidal particles, often caused by washing
trapping of foreign ions inside the growing lattice of a solid
the solution remaining after a solid has been separated
items.s: mother liquor: the solution remaining after a solid has been separated. The other options describe ignition, occlusion, peptisation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the quotient of the total amount concentration of a solute in the organic phase to that in the aqueous phase at equilibrium”
o: distribution ratio
stationary phase
chromatography
retention time
items.s: distribution ratio is the quotient of the total amount concentration of a solute in the organic phase to that in the aqueous phase at equilibrium.

items.q: Which term is described by “unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition”?
o: systematic error
confidence interval
random error
precision
items.s: random error is unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition.

items.q: Which of the following best describes arithmetic mean?
o: a result that lies so far from the others that it is suspected of belonging to a different population
the sum of the replicate results divided by the number of results
a bias that shifts every result in the same direction by a similar amount
a measure of the spread of replicate results about their centre, obtained from the square root of the variance
items.s: arithmetic mean: the sum of the replicate results divided by the number of results. The other options describe outlier, standard deviation, systematic error.

items.q: Which of the following best describes precision?
o: the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity determined
the closeness of replicate results to one another
a bias that shifts every result in the same direction by a similar amount
unpredictable scatter about the mean which cannot be eliminated but can be reduced by repetition
items.s: precision: the closeness of replicate results to one another. The other options describe random error, accuracy, systematic error.

items.q: peptisation may be defined as
o: an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
the unwanted inclusion of soluble impurities in a solid as it forms
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
the re-dispersion of a coagulated solid into colloidal particles, often caused by washing
items.s: peptisation: the re-dispersion of a coagulated solid into colloidal particles, often caused by washing. The other options describe precipitate, coprecipitation, digestion.

items.q: junction potential is best described as
o: the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity
a membrane sensor whose potential changes with the hydrogen ion activity of the solution
a technique in which the current at a fixed applied voltage is followed while reagent is added
the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet
items.s: junction potential: the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet. The other options describe amperometry, cell constant, glass electrode.

items.q: Which of the following best describes buffer capacity?
o: the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably
the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present
the stage at which the indicator changes colour, which is intended to coincide with complete reaction
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
items.s: buffer capacity: the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably. The other options describe dissociation constant, equivalence point, end point.

items.q: Which term is described by “the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution”?
o: titrant
normality
aliquot
molarity
items.s: molarity is the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution.

items.q: Which of the following best describes normality?
o: the mass of a substance that supplies or consumes one mole of reacting units such as hydrogen ions or electrons
one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent
the number of equivalent weights of solute present in one cubic decimetre of solution
items.s: normality: the number of equivalent weights of solute present in one cubic decimetre of solution. The other options describe parts per million, equivalent weight, molality.

items.q: Which of the following best describes primary standard?
o: the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution
one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
a highly pure stable substance weighed directly to prepare a solution of known strength
the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent
items.s: primary standard: a highly pure stable substance weighed directly to prepare a solution of known strength. The other options describe molarity, molality, parts per million.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines representative portion?
o: material whose composition matches the bulk within the uncertainty required by the method
the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted
a device that divides a flowing stream of powder into two equal portions over and over
heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance
items.s: representative portion: material whose composition matches the bulk within the uncertainty required by the method. The other options describe gross sample, drying to constant mass, riffle splitter.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines laboratory sample.
o: a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out
heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance
the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted
the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material
items.s: laboratory sample: the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material. The other options describe drying to constant mass, composite sample, gross sample.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines buffer solution.
o: the negative logarithm to base ten of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
a proton donor that is only partly ionised in aqueous solution, so an equilibrium mixture results
a mixture that resists a change in hydrogen ion level when small amounts of acid or alkali are added
the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present
items.s: buffer solution: a mixture that resists a change in hydrogen ion level when small amounts of acid or alkali are added. The other options describe weak acid, pH, equivalence point.

items.q: Beer-Lambert law is best described as
o: the statement that absorbance is proportional to concentration and to the length of the light path
the logarithm to base ten of the ratio of incident to transmitted radiant power
a plot of instrument response against the concentration of standards, used to convert measurements into amounts
the fraction of the incident radiant power that passes through the sample
items.s: Beer-Lambert law: the statement that absorbance is proportional to concentration and to the length of the light path. The other options describe absorbance, calibration curve, transmittance.

items.q: Which of the following best describes junction potential?
o: a half cell of constant known voltage against which the sensing half cell is measured
the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet
the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part
a technique in which the current at a fixed applied voltage is followed while reagent is added
items.s: junction potential: the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet. The other options describe amperometry, reference electrode, Nernst equation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines aliquot?
o: one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the mass of a substance that supplies or consumes one mole of reacting units such as hydrogen ions or electrons
a measured portion taken from a larger volume for a single determination
a highly pure stable substance weighed directly to prepare a solution of known strength
items.s: aliquot: a measured portion taken from a larger volume for a single determination. The other options describe equivalent weight, parts per million, primary standard.

items.q: Which term is described by “the mass of a substance that supplies or consumes one mole of reacting units such as hydrogen ions or electrons”?
o: primary standard
equivalent weight
aliquot
mass concentration
items.s: equivalent weight is the mass of a substance that supplies or consumes one mole of reacting units such as hydrogen ions or electrons.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the ratio of the molar mass of the sought substance to that of the weighed form, allowing for stoichiometry”
o: gravimetric analysis
mother liquor
precipitate
gravimetric factor
items.s: gravimetric factor is the ratio of the molar mass of the sought substance to that of the weighed form, allowing for stoichiometry.

items.q: Which term is described by “a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability”?
o: arithmetic mean
systematic error
confidence interval
outlier
items.s: confidence interval is a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines molality.
o: a highly pure stable substance weighed directly to prepare a solution of known strength
the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution
the reagent of known strength delivered from the burette during a volumetric determination
the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent
items.s: molality: the amount of solute in moles present in one kilogram of solvent. The other options describe molarity, primary standard, titrant.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a method in which iodine liberated by the analyte is measured with thiosulphate”
o: oxidation
iodometric titration
complexometric titration
conditional constant
items.s: iodometric titration is a method in which iodine liberated by the analyte is measured with thiosulphate.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance”
o: drying to constant mass
laboratory sample
gross sample
stratified portion
items.s: drying to constant mass is heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance.

items.q: monochromator is best described as
o: the wavelength at which two interconvertible species have equal absorptivity so absorbance does not change with their ratio
a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source
a transparent cell of fixed path length that holds the solution in the light beam
the absorbance of a solution of unit amount concentration measured in a cell of unit path length
items.s: monochromator: a device that isolates a narrow band of wavelengths from a polychromatic source. The other options describe isosbestic point, cuvette, molar absorptivity.

items.q: laboratory sample may be defined as
o: a blend of several increments taken at different positions so that local variation is averaged out
material whose composition matches the bulk within the uncertainty required by the method
the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted
the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material
items.s: laboratory sample: the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material. The other options describe composite sample, gross sample, representative portion.

items.q: distribution ratio is best described as
o: the quotient of the total amount concentration of a solute in the organic phase to that in the aqueous phase at equilibrium
the ratio of the time a component spends in the fixed bed to the time it spends in the moving fluid
the fixed material over which the moving fluid passes and with which components interact
a separation produced by the different rates at which components move through a fixed bed carried by a fluid
items.s: distribution ratio: the quotient of the total amount concentration of a solute in the organic phase to that in the aqueous phase at equilibrium. The other options describe retention factor, chromatography, stationary phase.

items.q: precipitate is best described as
o: the re-dispersion of a coagulated solid into colloidal particles, often caused by washing
an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
a method in which the analyte is converted into a sparingly soluble or volatile product that is weighed
keeping a solid in contact with its mother liquor so that small particles recrystallise into larger ones
items.s: precipitate: an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction. The other options describe digestion, gravimetric analysis, peptisation.

items.q: dissociation constant may be defined as
o: the negative logarithm to base ten of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably
a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution
items.s: dissociation constant: the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base. The other options describe strong acid, buffer capacity, pH.

items.q: drying to constant mass is best described as
o: material whose composition matches the bulk within the uncertainty required by the method
heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance
the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material
a small portion withdrawn at one point in space or time while material is being collected
items.s: drying to constant mass: heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance. The other options describe laboratory sample, representative portion, increment.

items.q: Which of the following best describes strong acid?
o: the negative logarithm to base ten of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present
a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution
items.s: strong acid: a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution. The other options describe equivalence point, pH, dissociation constant.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines quartering.
o: the large quantity removed from a consignment before any reduction is attempted
material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented
the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material
a reduction technique in which a flattened heap is divided into four parts and two opposite parts are retained
items.s: quartering: a reduction technique in which a flattened heap is divided into four parts and two opposite parts are retained. The other options describe laboratory sample, gross sample, stratified portion.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines increment.
o: material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented
the reduced quantity delivered to the analyst which must still match the bulk material
a reduction technique in which a flattened heap is divided into four parts and two opposite parts are retained
a small portion withdrawn at one point in space or time while material is being collected
items.s: increment: a small portion withdrawn at one point in space or time while material is being collected. The other options describe stratified portion, laboratory sample, quartering.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines retention volume?
o: the transfer of a solute from one liquid phase to another immiscible liquid
the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector
the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component
the fixed material over which the moving fluid passes and with which components interact
items.s: retention volume: the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector. The other options describe stationary phase, solvent extraction, retention time.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines equivalence point.
o: the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present
the equilibrium quotient for the splitting of a proton donor into its proton and its conjugate base
a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution
a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges
items.s: equivalence point: the stage of a titration at which the amount of titrant added exactly matches the amount of analyte present. The other options describe dissociation constant, strong acid, indicator.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines parts per million.
o: the quantity of solute in grams present in one cubic decimetre of solution
one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the mass of a substance that supplies or consumes one mole of reacting units such as hydrogen ions or electrons
the amount of solute in moles present in one cubic decimetre of solution
items.s: parts per million: one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material. The other options describe molarity, mass concentration, equivalent weight.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution”
o: strong acid
weak acid
end point
dissociation constant
items.s: strong acid is a proton donor that is completely ionised in dilute aqueous solution.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a half cell of constant known voltage against which the sensing half cell is measured”
o: potentiometry
Nernst equation
reference electrode
amperometry
items.s: reference electrode is a half cell of constant known voltage against which the sensing half cell is measured.

items.q: Which of the following best describes oxidation?
o: a dye that binds the cation under determination and gives up its colour once the titrant has taken that cation away
the electrode voltage of a half reaction measured with every species held at unit activity
the loss of electrons by a species, which increases its charge number
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
items.s: oxidation: the loss of electrons by a species, which increases its charge number. The other options describe metal indicator, complexometric titration, standard potential.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Nernst equation.
o: the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part
the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution
the ability of a solution to carry current, measured as the conductance of a cell of unit dimensions
a technique in which the current at a fixed applied voltage is followed while reagent is added
items.s: Nernst equation: the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part. The other options describe potentiometry, conductivity, amperometry.

items.q: Which of the following best describes end point?
o: the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably
a mixture that resists a change in hydrogen ion level when small amounts of acid or alkali are added
the stage at which the indicator changes colour, which is intended to coincide with complete reaction
a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges
items.s: end point: the stage at which the indicator changes colour, which is intended to coincide with complete reaction. The other options describe buffer solution, buffer capacity, indicator.

items.q: Which of the following best describes representative portion?
o: material taken separately from each distinct layer or zone of a heap so that every zone is represented
material whose composition matches the bulk within the uncertainty required by the method
heating and reweighing repeatedly until two successive weighings differ by less than the balance tolerance
a device that divides a flowing stream of powder into two equal portions over and over
items.s: representative portion: material whose composition matches the bulk within the uncertainty required by the method. The other options describe drying to constant mass, riffle splitter, stratified portion.

items.q: Which of the following best describes parts per million?
o: one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material
the number of equivalent weights of solute present in one cubic decimetre of solution
the reagent of known strength delivered from the burette during a volumetric determination
the quantity of solute in grams present in one cubic decimetre of solution
items.s: parts per million: one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material. The other options describe titrant, mass concentration, normality.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material”
o: titrant
normality
equivalent weight
parts per million
items.s: parts per million is one milligram of a substance present in one cubic decimetre of the material.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a proton donor that is only partly ionised in aqueous solution, so an equilibrium mixture results”
o: dissociation constant
buffer solution
weak acid
buffer capacity
items.s: weak acid is a proton donor that is only partly ionised in aqueous solution, so an equilibrium mixture results.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Nernst equation?
o: the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet
the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity
the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part
a half cell of constant known voltage against which the sensing half cell is measured
items.s: Nernst equation: the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part. The other options describe cell constant, junction potential, reference electrode.

items.q: Which of the following best describes standard potential?
o: a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
a dye that binds the cation under determination and gives up its colour once the titrant has taken that cation away
the loss of electrons by a species, which increases its charge number
the electrode voltage of a half reaction measured with every species held at unit activity
items.s: standard potential: the electrode voltage of a half reaction measured with every species held at unit activity. The other options describe masking agent, oxidation, metal indicator.

items.q: weak acid may be defined as
o: a weak acid or base whose two forms have different colours in different acidity ranges
the negative logarithm to base ten of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
the amount of added acid or alkali that a solution can absorb before its hydrogen ion level changes appreciably
a proton donor that is only partly ionised in aqueous solution, so an equilibrium mixture results
items.s: weak acid: a proton donor that is only partly ionised in aqueous solution, so an equilibrium mixture results. The other options describe buffer capacity, pH, indicator.

items.q: potentiometry may be defined as
o: the ability of a solution to carry current, measured as the conductance of a cell of unit dimensions
the small unwanted voltage set up where two solutions of different composition meet
the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution
the ratio of the distance between the electrodes to their area, used to convert conductance to conductivity
items.s: potentiometry: the measurement of the potential of a sensing electrode to obtain the activity of a species in solution. The other options describe junction potential, cell constant, conductivity.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity determined”
o: confidence interval
arithmetic mean
accuracy
systematic error
items.s: accuracy is the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity determined.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines theoretical plate?
o: the interval between injection of a sample and the appearance of the peak maximum of a component
a separation produced by the different rates at which components move through a fixed bed carried by a fluid
a hypothetical zone of the column in which one equilibration of solute between the phases is achieved
the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector
items.s: theoretical plate: a hypothetical zone of the column in which one equilibration of solute between the phases is achieved. The other options describe retention volume, chromatography, retention time.

items.q: The result of a determination is calculated as the product of two measured quantities whose relative uncertainties are 1.9 per cent and 2.6 per cent. Calculate the relative uncertainty of the result in per cent.
items.s: For a product the relative uncertainties combine in quadrature: sqrt(1.9^2 + 2.6^2) = 3.22 per cent.

items.q: A calibration line of absorbance against concentration passes through the standard points (0.004 mol/dm3, 0.227) and (0.02 mol/dm3, 0.983). A sample gives an absorbance of 0.605. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.

A 25 cm3 sample of a solution of an oxidising agent required 22.5 cm3 of sodium thiosulphate solution of concentration 0.141 mol/dm3. One mole of the agent liberates 1 mol of iodine and one mole of iodine consumes two moles of thiosulphate. Calculate the concentration of the agent in mol/dm3.
items.s: Thiosulphate used = 0.141 x 22.5/1000 = 0.0032 mol; iodine = half of that; agent = iodine/1, so the concentration is 0.063 mol/dm3.

items.q: 0.307 g of an impure sample of a base of molar mass 56 g/mol was treated with 25 cm3 of hydrochloric acid of concentration 0.124 mol/dm3 and the excess acid required 10.9 cm3 of sodium hydroxide of concentration 0.1 mol/dm3. Taking the reaction ratio as 1:1 throughout, calculate the percentage purity of the sample.
items.s: Acid taken = 0.0031 mol; excess = 0.0011 mol; acid consumed = 0.002 mol; mass of base = x 56 = 0.113 g, so purity = 36.66 per cent.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 50 cm3 containing a solute is shaken once with 10 cm3 of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 12. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase.
items.s: Fraction remaining = Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 50/(50 + 12 x 10) = 0.294.

items.q: Five replicate titrations on the same solution gave the volumes 26.36, 29.94, 26.26, 24.16, 23.21 cm3. Calculate the mean titre in cm3.
items.s: Mean = sum of the five volumes divided by five = 25.99 cm3.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of copper in an alloy gave the percentages 14.14, 14.61, 16.44, 16.59, 17.62. Calculate the median percentage.
items.s: Arranged in order the values are 14.14, 14.61, 16.44, 16.59, 17.62, so the middle value is 16.44 per cent.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of iron in an ore gave the percentages 13.41, 11.81, 10.87, 12.37, 14.43. Calculate the standard deviation of the results in per cent.
items.s: The mean is 12.58; the sum of squared deviations is 7.67; dividing by four and taking the root gives 1.38 per cent.

items.q: Six replicate measurements of a titre gave a mean of 24 cm3 and a standard deviation of 0.33 cm3. Calculate the relative spread of the results in per cent.
items.s: Relative spread = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (0.33/24) x 100 = 1.38 per cent.

items.q: A mean of 34 mg was obtained from 9 replicate determinations whose standard deviation was 0.85 mg. Taking the Student t value for the stated degrees of freedom as 2.26, calculate the half width of the 95 per cent confidence interval in mg.
items.s: Half width = t x standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 2.26 x 0.85 / sqrt(9) = 0.64 mg.

items.q: Four replicate results arranged in ascending order are 21, 25, 33 and 38. The first result is suspected of being an outlier. Using Q = gap / spread, calculate the rejection quotient.
items.s: Q = (second value - first value)/(largest - smallest) = (25 - 21)/(38 - 21) = 0.235.

items.q: A solution transmits 64 per cent of the radiation at 520 nm. Calculate its absorbance.
A solution has an absorbance of 0.12 at 460 nm. Calculate the percentage of the incident radiation transmitted.
items.s: Transmittance = 10^(-A) x 100 = 10^(-0.12) x 100 = 75.86 per cent.

items.q: A solution is 0.0002 mol/dm3 in a coloured species whose molar absorptivity is 4483 dm3 mol-1 cm-1; the absorbance was measured in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the absorbance.
items.s: A = absorptivity x concentration x path length = 4483 x 0.0002 x 1.00 = 1.03.

items.q: A solution of a species whose molar absorptivity is 2694 dm3 mol-1 cm-1 gives an absorbance of 0.896 in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: c = A / (absorptivity x path length) = 0.896 / (2694 x 1.00) = 0.0003 mol/dm3.

items.q: A solution of concentration 0.0005 mol/dm3 gives an absorbance of 0.385 in a cell of path length 0.5 cm. Calculate the molar absorptivity in dm3 mol-1 cm-1.
items.s: Absorptivity = A / (c x b) = 0.385 / (0.0005 x 0.5) = 1540 dm3 mol-1 cm-1.

items.q: A volume of 109 cm3 of a solution that is 0.153 mol/dm3 in a compound of molar mass 98 g/mol is evaporated to dryness. Calculate the mass of residue in g.
A mass of 1.89 g of a compound of molar mass 98 g/mol is dissolved in water and made up to 500 cm3. Calculate the molar concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles = 1.89/98 = 0.019; concentration = moles/(500/1000) = 0.039 mol/dm3.

items.q: 26 cm3 of a solution of concentration 0.206 mol/dm3 is diluted with water to a final volume of 500 cm3. Calculate the concentration of the diluted solution in mol/dm3.
A mass of 11.46 mg of an ion is present in 200 cm3 of solution. Calculate the concentration in parts per million, that is mg per dm3.
items.s: Concentration = 11.46 mg / (200/1000) dm3 = 57.3 ppm.

items.q: A standard solution of concentration 0.02 mol/dm3 is to be prepared in a 250 cm3 volumetric flask from a solid of molar mass 204.2 g/mol. Calculate the mass of solid required in g.
A titration required 34.2 cm3 of a titrant of concentration 0.196 mol/dm3. Calculate the amount of titrant used in moles.
items.s: Moles = concentration x volume in dm3 = 0.196 x 34.2/1000 = 0.0067 mol.

items.q: A 32 cm3 aliquot of a solution of concentration 0.212 mol/dm3 is taken. Calculate the amount of solute in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles = concentration x volume in cm3 = 0.212 x 32 = 6.78 mmol.

items.q: A solution has a pH of 4.27. Calculate the hydrogen ion concentration in mol/dm3.
items.s: Hydrogen ion concentration = 10^(-pH) = 10^(-4.27) = 5.37e-05 mol/dm3.

items.q: A buffer is made from a weak acid of pKa 5.99 and its sodium salt, the ratio of salt concentration to acid concentration being 2. Calculate the pH of the buffer.
items.s: pH = pKa + log(salt/acid) = 5.99 + log(2) = 6.29.

items.q: A buffer of pH 7.11 is required from a weak acid of pKa 6.21. Calculate the ratio of the concentration of the conjugate base to that of the acid.
items.s: From pH = pKa + log(ratio), log(ratio) = 7.11 - 6.21, so the ratio is 7.94.

items.q: A weak monobasic acid of concentration 0.1 mol/dm3 gives a hydrogen ion concentration of 0.008 mol/dm3. Calculate its acid dissociation constant.

50 cm3 of a solution of a strong monobasic acid required 20.8 cm3 of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.233 mol/dm3 for complete neutralisation. Calculate the concentration of the acid in mol/dm3.
items.s: Moles of alkali = 0.233 x 20.8/1000; since the ratio is 1:1, acid concentration = 0.233 x 20.8/50 = 0.097 mol/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 aliquot of a metal ion solution required 20.5 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.009 mol/dm3. Given a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the amount of metal ion in the aliquot in millimoles.
items.s: Millimoles of metal = millimoles of EDTA = 0.009 x 20.5 = 0.184 mmol.

items.q: A 200 cm3 sample of water required 18.5 cm3 of EDTA solution of concentration 0.007 mol/dm3. Taking the molar mass of calcium carbonate as 100 g/mol and a 1:1 combining ratio, calculate the hardness in mg of calcium carbonate per dm3.
items.s: Moles of calcium = 0.007 x 18.5/1000 = 0.0001 mol in 200 cm3; mass of calcium carbonate = 0.0001 x 100 = 0.013 g, which in one dm3 is 64.75 mg/dm3.

items.q: A 25.0 cm3 portion of an iron(II) solution required 17.2 cm3 of potassium permanganate solution of concentration 0.015 mol/dm3. One mole of permanganate oxidises five moles of iron(II). Calculate the amount of iron(II) in the portion in millimoles.
items.s: Moles of permanganate = 0.015 x 17.2/1000; iron(II) = 5 x that = 1.29 mmol.

items.q: The standard potential of a metal electrode of the type M2+/M is 0.74 V. Calculate the electrode potential when the metal ion concentration is 0.001 mol/dm3, taking the term 2.303RT/nF as 0.0296 V.
items.s: For a divalent metal E = E0 + (0.0296) log[M2+] = 0.74 + 0.0296 x log(0.001) = 0.651 V.

items.q: A sample of mass 0.885 g gave a precipitate of mass 0.434 g whose gravimetric factor is 0.3. Calculate the percentage of the analyte in the sample.
items.s: Mass of analyte = 0.434 x 0.3 = 0.13 g; percentage = (0.13/0.885) x 100 = 14.71 per cent.

items.q: A sample of an ore of mass 1.33 g gave on ignition 0.684 g of Fe2O3 of molar mass 159.7 g/mol, which contains two atoms of iron of molar mass 55.85 g/mol. Calculate the percentage of iron in the ore.
items.s: The gravimetric factor is 2 x 55.85/159.7 = 0.699, so iron = 0.684 x 0.699 = 0.478 g and the percentage is 35.97.

items.q: A precipitate of mass 0.432 g was obtained whose gravimetric factor, converting the weighed form to the sought substance, is 0.4. Calculate the mass of the sought substance in g.
items.s: Mass sought = mass weighed x gravimetric factor = 0.432 x 0.4 = 0.173 g.

items.q: Ignition of 0.807 g of a precipitate of molar mass 143.3 g/mol gave a weighable form that contains one atom of a metal of molar mass 107.9 g/mol. Calculate the mass of the metal in the precipitate, taking one mole of the metal per mole of the precipitate.
A conductivity cell of constant 2 cm-1 is filled with a solution whose conductance is 6.75 millisiemens. Calculate the conductivity in mS/cm.
items.s: Conductivity = conductance x cell constant = 6.75 x 2 = 13.5 mS/cm.

items.q: A solution of conductivity 1.76 mS/cm gives a conductance of 4.78 millisiemens in a conductivity cell. Calculate the cell constant in cm-1.
items.s: Cell constant = conductivity / conductance = 1.76 / 4.78 = 0.368 cm-1.

items.q: Two half cells have standard potentials of -0.37 V and 0.38 V. Calculate the standard cell potential obtained by coupling them.
items.s: The couple with the higher potential acts as the cathode, so the cell potential is 0.38 - (-0.37) = 0.75 V.

items.q: A glass electrode gives a potential that changes by 0.0592 V for each unit of pH. Calculate the change in potential in V when the pH of the solution changes from 2.6 to 5.6.
A solute has a retention time of 4.77 min on a column for which an unretained marker takes 0.79 min. Calculate the retention factor.
A peak with retention time 9.87 min has a base width of 1.23 min. Calculate the number of theoretical plates, using N = 16 (tR/w)^2.
Two peaks have retention times 5.56 min and 6.7 min and base widths 0.32 min and 0.49 min. Calculate the resolution.
Two solutes have retention factors of 1.66 and 3.32 on the same column. Calculate the selectivity factor.
items.s: Selectivity factor = k2/k1 = 3.32/1.66 = 2.

items.q: A standard solution of concentration 0.0021 mol/dm3 gives a peak area of 0.255 and a sample gives a peak area of 0.302 under the same conditions. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.
items.s: Concentration is proportional to area, so c = 0.0021 x 0.302/0.255 = 0.0025 mol/dm3.

items.q: The mean of 6 replicate determinations is 21.15 mg and their standard deviation is 0.67 mg, while the certified value for the material is 21.91 mg. Calculate the value of t.
items.s: t = |mean - certified| x sqrt(n) / standard deviation = 0.76 x sqrt(6) / 0.67 = 2.78.

items.q: The result of a determination is calculated as the product of two measured quantities whose relative uncertainties are 2.5 per cent and 2.5 per cent. Calculate the relative uncertainty of the result in per cent.
items.s: For a product the relative uncertainties combine in quadrature: sqrt(2.5^2 + 2.5^2) = 3.54 per cent.

items.q: A calibration line of absorbance against concentration passes through the standard points (0.001 mol/dm3, 0.169) and (0.005 mol/dm3, 0.599). A sample gives an absorbance of 0.384. Calculate the concentration of the sample in mol/dm3.

A 50 cm3 sample of a solution of an oxidising agent required 12.1 cm3 of sodium thiosulphate solution of concentration 0.081 mol/dm3. One mole of the agent liberates 2 mol of iodine and one mole of iodine consumes two moles of thiosulphate. Calculate the concentration of the agent in mol/dm3.
items.s: Thiosulphate used = 0.081 x 12.1/1000 = 0.001 mol; iodine = half of that; agent = iodine/2, so the concentration is 0.0049 mol/dm3.

items.q: 0.516 g of an impure sample of a base of molar mass 61 g/mol was treated with 25 cm3 of hydrochloric acid of concentration 0.196 mol/dm3 and the excess acid required 15.5 cm3 of sodium hydroxide of concentration 0.087 mol/dm3. Taking the reaction ratio as 1:1 throughout, calculate the percentage purity of the sample.
items.s: Acid taken = 0.0049 mol; excess = 0.0013 mol; acid consumed = 0.0036 mol; mass of base = x 61 = 0.217 g, so purity = 41.98 per cent.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 25 cm3 containing a solute is shaken once with 20 cm3 of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 5. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase.
items.s: Fraction remaining = Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 25/(25 + 5 x 20) = 0.2.

items.q: An aqueous solution of volume 25 cm3 containing a solute is shaken twice, each time with a fresh 10 cm3 portion of an immiscible organic solvent. The distribution ratio is 9. Calculate the fraction of the solute remaining in the aqueous phase after the two extractions.
items.s: Each extraction leaves Va/(Va + D x Vo) = 0.217, so after two the fraction is the square, 0.047.

items.q: Five replicate titrations on the same solution gave the volumes 29.79, 28.38, 26.83, 25.41, 26.16 cm3. Calculate the mean titre in cm3.
items.s: Mean = sum of the five volumes divided by five = 27.31 cm3.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of copper in an alloy gave the percentages 13.42, 14.29, 14.89, 16.25, 19.36. Calculate the median percentage.
items.s: Arranged in order the values are 13.42, 14.29, 14.89, 16.25, 19.36, so the middle value is 14.89 per cent.

items.q: Five replicate determinations of iron in an ore gave the percentages 15.55, 15.25, 17.98, 15.37, 17.63. Calculate the standard deviation of the results in per cent.
items.s: The mean is 16.36; the sum of squared deviations is 7.11; dividing by four and taking the root gives 1.33 per cent.

items.q: Six replicate measurements of a titre gave a mean of 21 cm3 and a standard deviation of 1.1 cm3. Calculate the relative spread of the results in per cent.
items.s: Relative spread = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (1.1/21) x 100 = 5.24 per cent.

items.q: A mean of 35 mg was obtained from 6 replicate determinations whose standard deviation was 0.72 mg. Taking the Student t value for the stated degrees of freedom as 2.78, calculate the half width of the 95 per cent confidence interval in mg.
items.s: Half width = t x standard deviation / sqrt(n) = 2.78 x 0.72 / sqrt(6) = 0.817 mg.

items.q: Four replicate results arranged in ascending order are 26, 27, 28 and 33. The first result is suspected of being an outlier. Using Q = gap / spread, calculate the rejection quotient.
items.s: Q = (second value - first value)/(largest - smallest) = (27 - 26)/(33 - 26) = 0.143.

items.q: A solution has an absorbance of 0.59 at 460 nm. Calculate the percentage of the incident radiation transmitted.
items.s: Transmittance = 10^(-A) x 100 = 10^(-0.59) x 100 = 25.7 per cent.

items.q: A solution is 0.0005 mol/dm3 in a coloured species whose molar absorptivity is 4072 dm3 mol-1 cm-1; the absorbance was measured in a cell of path length 1.00 cm. Calculate the absorbance.
items.s: A = absorptivity x concentration x path length = 4072 x 0.0005 x 1.00 = 2.08.

items.q: In this course, accuracy refers to
o: a result that lies so far from the others that it is suspected of belonging to a different population
a range about a measured mean within which the true value is expected to lie with a stated probability
the sum of the replicate results divided by the number of results
the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity determined
items.s: accuracy: the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity determined. The other options describe confidence interval, outlier, arithmetic mean.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains masking agent.
o: a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant
an ion or molecule that donates an electron pair to a central metal to form a coordination compound
the electrode voltage of a half reaction measured with every species held at unit activity
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
items.s: masking agent: a reagent that binds an interfering ion so that it no longer reacts with the titrant. The other options describe ligand, standard potential, complexometric titration.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines gravimetric factor?
o: an insoluble solid separated from a solution by a chemical reaction
the solution remaining after a solid has been separated
the unwanted inclusion of soluble impurities in a solid as it forms
the ratio of the molar mass of the sought substance to that of the weighed form, allowing for stoichiometry
items.s: gravimetric factor: the ratio of the molar mass of the sought substance to that of the weighed form, allowing for stoichiometry. The other options describe coprecipitation, mother liquor, precipitate.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains iodometric titration.
o: the electrode voltage of a half reaction measured with every species held at unit activity
a volumetric method in which the titrant forms a stable coordination compound with the metal being determined
a method in which iodine liberated by the analyte is measured with thiosulphate
the effective stability quotient of a coordination compound at a stated acidity, allowing for side reactions
items.s: iodometric titration: a method in which iodine liberated by the analyte is measured with thiosulphate. The other options describe standard potential, conditional constant, complexometric titration.

items.q: The correct meaning of solvent extraction is
o: the transfer of a solute from one liquid phase to another immiscible liquid
the amount of moving fluid passing through the bed between injection and the arrival of a peak at the detector
the quotient of the total amount concentration of a solute in the organic phase to that in the aqueous phase at equilibrium
a hypothetical zone of the column in which one equilibration of solute between the phases is achieved
items.s: solvent extraction: the transfer of a solute from one liquid phase to another immiscible liquid. The other options describe distribution ratio, theoretical plate, retention volume.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Nernst equation.
o: a technique in which the current at a fixed applied voltage is followed while reagent is added
a conducting path that joins two half cells while preventing their solutions from mixing
the relation between the potential of a half cell and the activities of the species taking part
